penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Automated social media history deletion requires maintaining working scrapers/browser automations per platform (Facebook, LinkedIn, etc.) that break constantly with platform UI changes — each breakage requires human debugging and repair, constituting per-platform manual fulfillment work.

rationale: Privacy-conscious professionals (lawyers, executives, job seekers) represent a real paying segment, and tools like TweetDelete prove willingness to pay for this category. However, the fatal operational issue is platform fragility: automated social media deletion tools break constantly as Facebook, LinkedIn, and others change their UIs and actively block scrapers — this creates a recurring human maintenance burden that kills the autonomy model. The buyer is also somewhat vague ('privacy-conscious individuals') rather than a tight B2B ICP, making targeted outreach harder. Without the penalty, it would be a borderline validate candidate; with the operational reality of constant scraper maintenance, it drops out.
solution_plan: The operational model for cross-platform social history deletion is fundamentally incompatible with a hands-off Claude factory: every platform update breaks the automation, requiring constant human engineering attention. A narrower, safer pivot — a 'social media audit report' that uses Claude to analyze publicly visible profiles and flags high-risk posts for manual deletion — would be buildable (no scraping required), but then it becomes a one-time report product at a low price point, not a recurring subscription. That pivot could be validated cheaply: a $19 one-time audit report, sold via a landing page, with Claude generating the report from a user-submitted profile URL. However, this is a significant scope reduction from the original opportunity.
notes: requires_human_fulfillment penalty applied due to scraper maintenance burden. buyer_clarity (5) would also fail the build gate floor of 6 if the total were high enough to consider building. The narrower 'audit report' pivot is worth a quick test if Youval is interested, but do not build a full automated deletion product.
